overview: 341-species fungus classifier, MobileNetV2 1.0/160 int8, 74.0% top-1 / 93.5% top-5. Not for edibility decisions.
usage:
# Not for edibility decisions

This model names a fungus species from a photo with the accuracy below, which means a wrong top-1 answer about one time in four. Never eat a mushroom on the strength of a classifier's output.

# Model Format

`fungi_int8.tflite`: full-integer TFLite, uint8 in and out, runs as is on TensorFlow Lite Micro and LiteRT. `fungi_int8_edgetpu.tflite`: compiled with Edge TPU compiler 16.0, every op mapped. `fungi_float32.tflite`: float in and out. `labels.txt`: one class per line, "Latin name (Common name)", line number = class index. `classes.json`: full taxonomy per class.

# Training Data

iNaturalist 2021 competition train split, 90,048 images of 341 fungus species (including 55 lichens). Initialised from timm's ImageNet mobilenetv2_100.ra_in1k. 12 epochs, random resized crops, flips, colour jitter.

# Model Inputs

[1, 160, 160, 3] uint8 RGB, 0 to 255, no normalization (the model rescales internally). Centre-crop to a square; an 87.5% centre crop (short side to 183, crop 160) matches validation.

# Model Outputs

[1, 341] uint8 probabilities, scale 1/256 and zero point 0 (prob = value / 256). No background class.

# Model Usage

Measured on the int8 file over the 3,410 iNat2021 val images for these species: 74.0% top-1 / 93.5% top-5. Any tf.lite.Interpreter works; the GitHub README has a runnable snippet and scripts (classify.py, webcam.py, eval_tflite.py). Full hardware notes: https://github.com/mlgraham/species-classifiers#deployment-contract

# Fine-tuning

Re-train with scripts/distill.py in the GitHub repository; the recipe and what was measured not to help are documented there.

# Changelog

v1: matches GitHub release v0.1.0 (sha256 in SHA256SUMS.txt there) and Hugging Face mlgraham/species-classifier-fungi.
